elephant.a: A trunk is a long nose and top lip joined together. Elephants use it to breathe, smell, drink and pick things up.

elephant.q: Why do elephants have big ears?
elephant.a: Big floppy ears let heat escape, keeping an elephant cool in hot sun. Ears also help elephants hear sounds far away.

elephant.q: Why do elephants spray dust on themselves?
elephant.a: Dust and mud make a cool coat that stops sunburn and keeps bugs away. Elephants toss it on with their trunks.
Elephants have very good memories for faces, places and family. Remembering where water is helps a whole herd survive.

lion.a: A big furry mane makes a lion look bigger and stronger to other lions. It also keeps his neck safe when lions play fight.

lion.q: Why do lions sleep so much?
lion.a: Hunting takes lots of energy, so a lion naps to save it up. Most lions sleep for a big part of the day.

lion.q: Why do lions live in groups?
lion.a: A lion family is called a pride. Living together helps them hunt, share food and look after the cubs.

lion.q: Why do lions roar so loudly?
lion.a: A roar can be heard far across the land. It warns other lions that this space already belongs to someone.

giraffe.q: Why do giraffes have long necks?
giraffe.a: A long neck helps a giraffe reach juicy leaves at the top of tall trees. It also helps them spot danger from far away.

giraffe.q: Why do giraffes have long tongues?
giraffe.a: A long dark tongue can curl round thorny branches without getting hurt. It grabs leaves that other animals cannot reach.

giraffe.q: Why do giraffes sleep standing up?
giraffe.a: Standing lets a giraffe jump up fast if danger comes near. Giraffes only need a little sleep, often in short naps.

giraffe.q: Why do giraffes have small horns?
giraffe.a: Both boy and girl giraffes have two furry bumps on their heads. They use them to gently bump each other when play fighting.

zebra.a: Every zebra has its own pattern of stripes, like a fingerprint. Stripes may also confuse hungry lions by blurring together in a running herd.

zebra.q: Why do zebras live in herds?
zebra.a: A big group has many eyes watching for danger, so zebras feel safer together. Herds also help zebras find water and grass.

zebra.q: Why do zebras have short manes?
zebra.a: A short stiff mane stands up along their neck and does not flop in their eyes. It still helps them show their mood.

zebra.q: Why do baby zebras stay close to mum?
zebra.a: A newborn foal learns its mother's own stripe pattern within days, so it never loses her in a big herd. Staying close also keeps it safe from lions.

monkey.q: Why do monkeys live in trees?
monkey.a: Trees keep monkeys safe from animals that cannot climb. Branches also give them fruit, leaves and a comfy place to nap.
Many monkeys use their tail like a spare hand for gripping branches. A good grip means they will not fall while climbing high.

monkey.q: Why do monkeys groom each other?
monkey.a: Picking through fur removes bugs and dirt, and it feels nice too. Grooming is also how monkey friends and families show they care.

monkey.q: Why do monkeys chatter and screech?
monkey.a: Loud calls warn the whole troop when danger like a snake or eagle is near. Different calls can mean different kinds of danger.
